scope: Reconcile the stale screenshot sanitizer issue row against current code and maintained tests

prior_art.review_finding: Cycle023's implementation and test receipt repair the behavior described as still broken in the RF060 register row.
prior_art.source_behavior: Oversized encoded images are omitted with an explicit reason, caller-owned screenshot and notes are copied before shaping, full PNG/JPEG decode rejects malformed and truncated streams, storage receipts validate object name/URL/size, and required capture failure is persisted and returned.

fault_cases: valid storage receipt and byte-for-byte readback
empty URL/object name and wrong size
invalid image, truncated PNG and over-budget image
current_verification.oracles: Caller screenshot bytes/dimensions/media type and caller notes remain unchanged; successful stored bytes match the encoded input and decode; failed required capture persists a failed outcome without publishing an image URL.

tracking.problem_register: BAS-RF-060 now records the integrity behavior as resolved, cites both the original receipt and this current rerun, and retains resource/latency qualifications as separate limitations.
tracking.feedback: BAS-FB-008 is unchanged and already retained verbatim; no duplicate entry was added.

known_limits.historical_isolated_benchmark: Cycle023 complete image validation measured median writer time 32.071ms to 38.079ms (+18.7%) and allocations about113KB/op to3.863MB/op; exact numbers and workload are retained in screenshot-storage-2026-09-22.json.
known_limits.hostile_dimensions: No decoded-pixel memory bound or hostile-dimension resource receipt exists.
known_limits.product_impact: The current capture workload remains 419ms service p95 under its 2000ms budget; the writer-only benchmark does not prove an end-to-end regression or improvement.

next_review: Only add a pixel/memory limit if it can be derived from a declared resource budget and retained browser/image capabilities.
